items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the election law, in relation to the accessibility of
congressional, senatorial, assembly and election district maps
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4591

SPONSOR: SKOUFIS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the election law, in relation to the accessibility of
congressional, senatorial, assembly and election district maps

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To require boards of elections to publish election district maps in
Shapefile format on their website.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends section 4-102 of the election law by adding a new para-
graph to require that election district maps shall be posted on board of
elections' website and each board of elections shall make such maps
available in a downloadable Shapefile format.

Section 2 provides the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Election districts and the process of drawing new boundaries has been an
arcane process for the vast majority of voters. Election district maps
are only accessible to the public by viewing hard copies at the clerk's
office. For many people, that is not feasible or practical because indi-
viduals must travel there in person and the maps are not in a user-
friendly format. The lack of transparency related to election district
maps leave voters unable to voice concerns about the way in which
election districts are created. As a result, many voters believe
election district boundaries are created through a manipulative process
that legislators utilize for their own political gain. However, granting
voters access to election district maps may allow for people to suggest
alternatives that are less partisan and pressure decision makers to draw
the districts more fairly in the first place.

This bill would require each board of elections to publish the appropri-
ate election district maps on their website. These maps would also be
made available in a Shapefile format, which enables members of the
public to download the map and utilize geographic information system
(GIS) software.

The redistricting process is an inherently geographic undertaking
because each year, the geographic distribution of a community changes as
people are born, retire, or relocate. If election district maps are
available in Shapefile format, they are compatible with GIS soft- ware
that enables people to see what effect boundary changes will have on a
community or population. Additionally, GIS software can utilize census
data or other datasets that allow users to measure compliance of specif-
ic redistricting principles like population size and diversity. There-
fore, the availability of election district maps iASHapefile format
would allow voters to review the demographics of districts and hold
legislators accountable when boundaries are unfairly drawn.

 
PRIOR. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

A.10330a of 2020, referred to election law FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:  None.
 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
